subject: Cartella fanout spike — mitigation steps, product asks, and customer runbook
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tim Blake <tim@cartella.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: [INCIDENT] Cartella: sudden p99 token fanout around 07:50 PT

Folks —

Alert fired at ~07:50 PT: Cartella (prod-us-west) saw a ~6x jump in p99 for streaming/generation endpoints and a concurrent throughput fall on their checkout route. Early signs point to a fanout pattern from a new client-side change that aggressively parallelizes requests (many short prompts).

Immediate ask: can SRE/E2E throttle at the routing layer to give us breathing room while we triage? Tim, are you able to pause the rollout from your side?

I've attached a snapshot and the prefix eviction log from the runtime.

-Ben

Attachment: latency-snapshot-20280527.png (PNG, 483KB)
Attachment: prefix-kv-eviction.log (TXT, 1.2MB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tim Blake <tim@cartella.com>
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@cartella.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T08:32:00-07:00
Subject: RE: [INCIDENT] Cartella: sudden p99 token fanout around 07:50 PT

Thanks Ben — good catch. Quick coordination plan: 

1) Rishi / SRE: please put a soft throttle on cartella-prod route (route-id: cartella-checkout-v2) to limit per-client concurrent in-flight requests to 3 and cap streaming parallelism to 2 for the next 60 minutes. We want time to validate root cause before broader action.
2) Product ask: Jonas, can you confirm whether we can expose a temporary routing knob (customer-scoped) to reduce streaming concurrency? If not, can we do a deploy-safe feature flag?
3) Customer comms: Marissa/Ben — draft a short runbook we can send to Cartella ops (what they should pause, what we will do). Keep it prescriptive.
4) Engineering triage: Rishi, please attach any kernel/quantization regressions you see; note whether this is cache eviction related.

Tim/Elena — we recommend pausing the new parallelization rollout for now. We will follow with a short runbook with steps to stabilize.

I'll own the customer-facing runbook and send a single note once we have the commands to pause.

-Neha

Signature:
Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tim Blake <tim@cartella.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: [INCIDENT] Cartella: sudden p99 token fanout around 07:50 PT

Quick findings from the first 20m of triage: 
- The runtime shows rapid prefix/KV eviction activity concurrent with the spike; memory pressure increased on those pods. Evictions correlate with a lot of short-lived sessions that don't re-use KV caches.
- We saw a kernel scheduling hotspot on multi-tenant pools serving cartella-checkout-v2 (nv_core_schedule starved for ~120s windows).
- No new model load or quantization change detected in the past 72h for this customer.

Mitigation steps I am executing now: 
- placing a soft token-based admission control on cartella-checkout-v2 (limit-per-tenant=3, backlog=10) — applied to the edge routing policy.
- reducing batch_window_ms from 40 -> 20 on the dedicated pool handling this route to reduce head-of-line latency for short prompts.

Product ask (short): a customer-scoped concurrency knob at the route level (admin-configurable) that caps streaming concurrency and sets a fallback model variant when concurrency exceeds threshold. This would let us avoid global throttles.

I will produce a short telemetry snapshot (sampling of 1% of traces) and upload to the Drive link in 30m.

-Rishi

Signature:
Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead — Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tim Blake <tim@cartella.com>, Elena Torres <elena@cartella.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: [INCIDENT] Cartella: sudden p99 token fanout around 07:50 PT

Draft customer runbook (short):

Subject: Immediate action for Cartella — steps to stabilize checkout latency
Hi Tim / Elena,

Thanks for working with us on this. Below are the immediate steps to stabilize your checkout flows while we triage the root cause: 

1) Pause the new parallelization rollout (client SDK): disable the parallelRequest flag in feature rollout v3 for 20 minutes.
2) If you see 429s: reduce client-side concurrency to 2 and add exponential backoff (initial 100ms).
3) Send us a short trace for any request exceeding 1.5s (we'll provide a curl+header example).
4) If you can, temporarily route heavy batch inference to your non-streaming endpoint (we will provide the endpoint).

What Redwood will do: apply temporary concurrency limits on your route, reduce batch window on the serving pool, and share a sampled trace set + remediation checklist within 60m.

We recommend the two teams reconvene after stabilization for a postmortem and product follow-up.

Would you like this as a one-page runbook or a step-by-step checklist?

-Marissa

Signature:
Marissa Cole
Customer Reliability Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Tim Blake <tim@cartella.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T11:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: [INCIDENT] Cartella: sudden p99 token fanout around 07:50 PT

A couple of product clarifications on the ask for a "customer-scoped concurrency knob":

- We already have a global throttle config but not exposed per-customer via the console. Exposing it will require: console UI change, RBAC guardrails, and a short API (admin-only) to set per-tenant limits. Estimated effort: 2 sprints to ship a safe UI + API.
- Short-term: we can add an admin-only route-level API that SRE can call to set per-tenant concurrency caps. No UI; CLI/API only. I can prioritize that as a hotfix (one engineer + one QA for a week).

Jonas
Product Manager — Serving

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Tim Blake <tim@cartella.com>, Elena Torres <elena@cartella.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-27T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Stabilization checklist — Cartella checkout (what to pause + what Redwood did)

Hi Tim / Elena —

Thank you for pausing the client rollout and for quick responses. Below is a short checklist we ran together and the actions Redwood applied: 

What Cartella did (confirmed):
- toggled off parallelRequest in v3 rollout at 08:57 PT
- reduced client concurrency to 2

What Redwood applied (completed):
- soft tenant-level admission control: concurrent_inflight_per_tenant=3 (applied 08:44 PT)
- reduced batch_window_ms on the dedicated serving pool for cartella-checkout-v2 to 20ms (applied 08:50 PT)
- increased tracing sampling to 1% for this route and uploaded sampled traces to Drive (link above)
- SRE placed short-term migration of high-QPS requests to a less contended pool for 45m (rolling change)

Next steps / product asks: 
- Jonas: please prioritize the admin API to set per-tenant concurrency caps as a hotfix (one-week ETA).
- Postmortem: schedule a joint review with Eng + Customer Reliability to determine if we need a persistent per-tenant knob or improved client-side guidance.

Attached is a one-page runbook (cartella-maup-runbook-v1.md) with the exact commands we used and a curl example to send traces. We'll follow up with a brief postmortem once the sampled traces are analyzed.

If anything reoccurs, please page the on-call SRE and loop me in.

Neha

Signature:
Neha Kapoor
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
